intro: CTR tells you what share of the people who saw your ad actually clicked it. Enter clicks and impressions below to get the rate.

sections.heading: How CTR is calculated
sections.body: CTR is clicks divided by impressions, shown as a percentage. Impressions are how many times the ad was shown; clicks are how many of those views turned into a click. Nothing else feeds into it — no cost, no conversions, just the ratio of the two counts you already have in any ad platform's dashboard.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: An ad that gets 240 clicks from 12,000 impressions has a CTR of 2.00%. Double the impressions with the same click count and CTR halves — it moves with the denominator just as much as the numerator, which is easy to forget when comparing two campaigns that ran at different scales.

sections.heading: CTR and CTOR are not the same rate
sections.body: CTR divides clicks by impressions — everyone who was shown the ad, whether they noticed it or not. Click-to-Open Rate (CTOR) divides clicks by opens, and only applies to email, where 'opened' is a separate, earlier event than 'was delivered.' A campaign can have a low CTR but a healthy CTOR if the creative works once someone actually opens it — the two numbers are answering different questions, not two versions of the same one.

seo.seoDescription: Calculate click-through rate from clicks and impressions, with a worked example and the distinction between CTR and CTOR.
